page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 8 shared vCPUs and 8 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU hardware. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core CPU score in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling within the middle 50%. Memory performance is mixed; while memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, the PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is also weak at 6.02 GB/sec.

This instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that can leverage multi-threaded execution without requiring dedicated CPU resources or local storage. It is suitable for multi-threaded decompression, basic software compilation, and lightweight database operations, where its average Redis SET performance of 11.84 million operations per second can be utilized. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks, high-throughput web serving, or medium-to-large language model inference, where text generation speeds drop to poor levels.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data reveals a contrast between its poor single-core CPU performance and its average multi-core and multi-threaded capabilities, such as software compilation and bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth remains average, though overall memory performance and static web serving throughput are weak. This server represents a budget-friendly option for resource-dense, multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores, such as background processing, basic database operations, and development environments.
